video.title: New Orleans Pelicans Season Preview - A Team With No Direction

summary: Josh Lloyd and Jake Madison preview the New Orleans Pelicans, who had a very quiet offseason. Jake argues the team is stuck between two timelines: a win-now core of Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy and Herb Jones, and a rebuild core of Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen. They say Zion and Queen do not fit together, the roster lacks shooting and defensive rebounding, and Dejounte Murray blocks Fears from a lead guard role. Yves Missi is named as the player most likely to gain a bigger role, possibly as the starting center under new coach Jamahl Mosley's defense-first scheme. Jake sees this as a make or break year for Zion and predicts about 34 wins. A Trey Murphy trade is possible only if a team makes a huge offer.

rules.text: Rookies and second-year players usually do not help a team win. The leap tends to come in year three, so teams trying to win often bench their young players.
rules.quote: rookies don't help you win games. Secondyear players don't really help you win games. It's that third year

rules.text: A player on a cheap contract is worth the most in trades early in the deal. His trade value drops as his next contract gets closer.
rules.quote: the closer you get to having to pay him his next deal, the value goes down.

rules.text: Defensive scheme can affect a big man's rebounding. A switch-everything scheme pulls centers out to the perimeter and lowers their defensive rebounding rate.
rules.quote: So, I do think scheme can maybe help him a little bit

rules.text: Teams that keep competing late in the season can pile up wins in March and April against teams that are tanking.
rules.quote: they were able to rack up those wins in that period of the year when everyone else was trying to lose

player_notes.text: Zion is not a good rebounder. He does not space the floor or play defense.
player_notes.quote: They don't play defense. Zion's not a good rebounder. Queen could be a good enough rebounder here.

player_notes.text: He stayed healthy last season but had one of his worst years.
player_notes.quote: he was healthy last year, but he also probably had his like one of his worst years in the NBA

player_notes.text: Last season he was used off the ball more instead of as a point forward. The speaker thinks that is probably part of why he stayed healthy.
player_notes.quote: used him off ball more, not his, not the point Zion. And that's part probably part of the reason why he stayed healthy

player_notes.text: Year eight is a make or break season for him. He is the player under the most pressure on the team.
player_notes.quote: it's going to be year eight for him. If it's not make or break, when is it going to be?

player_notes.text: Queen and Fears were moved to the bench last season while the team chased the play-in.
player_notes.quote: reason you saw Derek Queen and Jeremiah Fears moved to the bench last year

player_notes.text: Queen had terrible first halves but put up big 12-minute runs in fourth quarters. He gives little rim protection or defense.
player_notes.quote: Queen puts up these numbers and he has these horrific first halves and he was putting up like ridiculous 12minute runs

player_notes.text: He is a hub big who works from the elbows and free throw line, not a three-point spacer.
player_notes.quote: Derek Queen is not a guy that's playing at the top of the three-point line as a big.

player_notes.text: Fears is a downhill lead guard who keeps attacking the rim even when he is not scoring there.
player_notes.quote: Zero fears is the mentality he plays with because he keeps getting to the rim.

player_notes.text: He is not a good enough three-point shooter to play off the ball as a two guard. He is also slightly undersized and not a good defender.
player_notes.quote: he's not a good enough three-point shooter where you can use him as a two guard like that

player_notes.text: Dejounte Murray will start over Fears, which limits his lead guard role.
player_notes.quote: Murray is certainly going to start over Jeremiah fears. If there's any decision it's going to be Deonte Murray.

player_notes.text: He is coming off an ACL injury and played only a handful of games last season, so he has little trade value.
player_notes.quote: he was coming off that injury, uh, the ACL, you know, he only played in a handful of games last year

player_notes.text: Murray is not a lights-out shooter. He can make threes but does not space the floor.
player_notes.quote: is this actually the best fit given that he's not a shooter either?

player_notes.text: The speakers call him an average to slightly above average player. A full season from him adds about one or two wins.
player_notes.quote: he's also not the type of guy that's giving you six plus wins a season

player_notes.text: Missi is the player most likely to see a big role change under the new regime and could become the starting center. Jake would start him over Queen on opening night.
player_notes.quote: have like the biggest role change under this new regime and come in and potentially be the starting center

player_notes.text: His shot blocking and rim protection improved a lot last season. He contested shots at the rim at a high rate.
player_notes.quote: his shot blocking was pretty good last year, truthfully.

player_notes.text: He is a poor defensive rebounder for a center, around the bottom 10% at his position. Less switching under Mosley could help.
player_notes.quote: He's not a great defensive rebounder in terms of just raw percentages here.

player_notes.text: His trade value is at its peak because of his team-friendly contract. The Pelicans reportedly want about three first-round picks and a young player for him.
player_notes.quote: because Trey Murphy's value is probably the highest it'll ever be right now.

player_notes.text: He shot about 42% from three two years ago but is not a true floor spacer.
player_notes.quote: we've seen Herb Jones two years ago shoot like 42% from three, but but that doesn't make you a court spacer

team_notes.text: The team is stuck between a win-now timeline and a rebuild timeline and will not commit to either one.
team_notes.quote: They're kind of stuck between two timelines in my opinion.

team_notes.text: Projected starters are Dejounte Murray, Herb Jones, Trey Murphy, Zion Williamson and probably Derik Queen. Center is a question mark.
team_notes.quote: Dejonte Murray, Herb Jones, Trey Murphy, Zion Williamson, and probably Derek Queen.
